title: Axitinib for kidney cancer
context_label: Advanced clear-cell renal cell carcinoma after prior sunitinib or a cytokine
indication_text: Advanced clear-cell renal cell carcinoma after prior sunitinib or a cytokine
purpose: Help control advanced kidney cancer after previous treatment.
schedule_summary: The usual starting dose is 5 mg by mouth twice daily, about 12 hours apart, with or without food. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerable; there is no planned week off. Your prescription may use a different dose.
administration_text: The usual starting dose is 5 mg by mouth twice daily, about 12 hours apart, with or without food. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerable; there is no planned week off. Your prescription may use a different dose.

agents.name: Axitinib
agents.type: Targeted therapy: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.mechanism: Axitinib blocks vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFRs), signals that help tumours grow new blood vessels. Reducing this blood supply can slow cancer growth. The same action explains effects on blood pressure, kidneys, bleeding and wound healing.
agents.explanation: Axitinib blocks vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFRs), signals that help tumours grow new blood vessels. Reducing this blood supply can slow cancer growth. The same action explains effects on blood pressure, kidneys, bleeding and wound healing.
risks: High blood pressure, sometimes severe; rare heart failure, heart attack, stroke or clots
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, constipation, reduced appetite and weight loss
Sore mouth, taste changes, fatigue and voice changes
Painful, red or peeling palms and soles; rash and dry skin
Thyroid changes, liver-test abnormalities and protein in the urine
Bleeding, occasionally serious; rare bowel perforation or abnormal connections (fistulas)
Delayed wound healing; rare reversible brain swelling syndrome (PRES)
Anaemia and changes in other blood cells; possible fertility and pregnancy harm
agents.watch: Collect a prescription for diarrhoea medicine, usually loperamide, before starting. Follow the supplied instructions and contact the team for persistent diarrhoea, dizziness, poor intake or reduced urine.

anatomy: Headache or fatigue may reflect pressure or thyroid changes. Sudden severe headache, confusion, seizures or visual loss needs emergency care.
Soreness, taste or voice changes can affect eating. Report pain or difficulty swallowing; use your mouth-care plan.
Measure blood pressure as advised. Chest pain, severe breathlessness or stroke symptoms need emergency care.
Blood tests may show liver irritation. Report yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or pain under the right ribs.
Diarrhoea and nausea can cause dehydration. Use prescribed support and call for persistent symptoms, bleeding or severe abdominal pain.
Protein can leak into urine. Report swelling, foamy urine, much less urine or dehydration.
Painful palms or soles can limit walking and daily tasks. Moisturise and report soreness before it becomes severe.
Report unusual bleeding or slow wound healing. A swollen painful leg, coughing blood or sudden breathlessness needs urgent assessment.

items.title: Evidence in this setting
items.text: In AXIS, 723 patients with previously treated advanced renal cell carcinoma received axitinib or sorafenib. The current EMA table reports median progression-free survival of 6.8 versus 4.7 months (hazard ratio 0.67; 95% confidence interval 0.56–0.81). Overall survival was not significantly different. Results varied with previous therapy; this does not compare axitinib with every current combination.

items.title: Your priorities
